Risk Statement: A credential-stuffing attacker may use the single-factor staff login design to gain unauthorized access to ClinicCloud and patient records.
Target Residual Risk: Enable MFA, enforce phishing-resistant authentication for privileged users, and monitor sign-in anomalies; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.1 authentication; §3.5 MFA open item

Risk Statement: A thief may use a stolen clinic laptop or active browser session because endpoint management and session protections are not defined, exposing ClinicCloud records.
Existing Controls: Clinic-owned Windows laptops; Chrome browser; vendor roles
Target Residual Risk: Require device baseline, full-disk encryption, screen lock, remote wipe, and short session timeout; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.1 devices; §3.4 no endpoint control stated

Risk Statement: A malicious or curious clinician may view patients from another clinic because ClinicCloud roles do not yet enforce clinic-level segmentation.
Existing Controls: Clinician and Front Desk roles exist; no location distinction
Target Residual Risk: Design and test clinic-level tenant or row-level access restrictions and quarterly access reviews; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.1 roles and §3.5 clinic-level segmentation open item

Risk Statement: Malware on an unmanaged, aging Windows laptop may steal credentials or disrupt access to ClinicCloud because patch status is unknown.
Target Residual Risk: Deploy supported endpoint protection, patch compliance, least privilege, and browser hardening before access; High
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.1 devices; §3.4 no network segmentation

Risk Statement: An unauthorized party may access legacy CSV exports in the shared migration folder because retention, disposal, access ownership, and post-import removal are not defined.
Existing Controls: HTTPS upload to vendor-provided folder; one-time bulk import
Target Residual Risk: Encrypt files before transfer, restrict folder access, log downloads, validate import, and securely delete exports after sign-off; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.2 migration flow; §3.3 CSV classification; §3.5 retention open item

Risk Statement: A migration operator or process error may corrupt or mis-map patient records during the one-time bulk import because validation, reconciliation, and segregation of duties are not specified.
Existing Controls: Vendor migration team and bulk import pipeline are planned
Target Residual Risk: Use a controlled migration runbook, checksums, reconciliation totals, sample validation, rollback copy, and dual approval; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.1 data migration; §3.2 migration pipeline

Risk Statement: A compromised or misconfigured third-party integration may disclose patient or billing data because clearinghouse and reminder-service data sharing is not covered by a security addendum or minimization review.
Target Residual Risk: Document data minimization, API authentication, allowlists, contract terms, and periodic integration reviews; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.2 integrations; §3.4 vendor contract gap

Risk Statement: A vendor compromise or regional outage may expose or make unavailable nightly backups because encryption, key ownership, and backup region are unspecified.
Existing Controls: Automated nightly backup is planned; encryption status unconfirmed
Target Residual Risk: Make backup encryption, region, restore testing, and notification commitments contractual and verify restore evidence; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.2 backup flow; §3.4 encryption and region open item

Risk Statement: An attacker or insider may access records without timely detection because audit logs remain inside ClinicCloud and MedCore has not designed access to them.
Existing Controls: Possible vendor-platform logs; no MedCore access or monitoring
Target Residual Risk: Contract for log export, define alerting and retention, and review privileged and patient-record access; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.4 logging and monitoring gap

Risk Statement: MedCore may fail to contain and notify a breach within required timelines because no incident-response or breach-notification procedure exists.
Target Residual Risk: Approve an incident-response plan with vendor contacts, evidence handling, decision points, notification roles, and exercises; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.4 incident-response gap; regulatory context §2

Risk Statement: A supplier failure or control weakness may compromise MedCore data because no vendor risk assessment or security addendum is complete for the SaaS and connected services.
Existing Controls: Vendor states ClinicCloud is ISO 27001 certified; certificate not provided
Target Residual Risk: Complete due diligence, obtain assurance reports/certificate, define breach SLA and right-to-audit, and track findings; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.4 vendor assurance and contract gaps

Risk Statement: A compromised helpdesk contractor account or unsafe remote-access tool may provide entry to clinic workstations because the tool and access controls are not selected.
Existing Controls: Contractor provides troubleshooting; remote tool not selected
Target Residual Risk: Select an audited tool with MFA, just-in-time access, session recording, approvals, and contractor offboarding; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.2 remote access; §3.5 tool open item

Risk Statement: Password spraying may compromise staff accounts because the only confirmed policy is the vendor default of eight characters with no confirmed complexity or rotation rule.
Existing Controls: Vendor default password minimum; no MedCore policy
Target Residual Risk: Adopt a password policy, prohibit reuse, require breached-password screening, rate limiting, and MFA; Low

Risk Statement: A public-internet or ClinicCloud outage may interrupt care and scheduling because all clinics depend on browser access to one external SaaS platform and no alternate link is planned.
Existing Controls: TLS 1.2 in transit; nightly backup planned
Target Residual Risk: Define vendor availability commitments, downtime procedures, local emergency access, communications, and recovery tests; Medium
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.1 public internet access; §3.2 data flow

Risk Statement: Former migration or integration access may persist after the relevant activity because no offboarding process is defined for the folder, reminder service, or clearinghouse.
Existing Controls: One-time migration and planned integrations; no offboarding process
Target Residual Risk: Create access inventory, expiry dates, termination checklist, and owner attestations for all temporary and third-party access; Low

Risk Statement: Legacy exports may be copied, altered, or retained beyond need during migration because the CSV lifecycle and integrity verification are not written.
Existing Controls: CSV export and HTTPS upload are planned
Target Residual Risk: Classify CSV as Restricted, use checksum and chain-of-custody records, limit copies, and document secure disposal approval; Low
Source/Evidence: Resource Pack §3.2 migration flow; §3.3 CSV open classification
